description: Zeenah is the Team Lead and Tech Lead for SonicSpace, an accessibility-focused project built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. As a developer and innovator, she specializes in translating complex Earth observation data into intuitive, multi-sensory experiences. Driven by a mission to make STEM and space data accessible to everyone including the visually impaired Zeenah is leading the architecture of SonicSpace's sonification engine and interactive frontend.
summary:
Sonic Space "Hear the Planet Change" project is an interactive, sonification app that transforms NASA Earth visualizations into synchronized audio experiences, addressing the accessibility gap in traditional visual science communication, particularly for blind and low-vision individuals.

The platform uses Python, NumPy, Pillow, and FFmpeg to process NASA visualization frames and extract environmental features such as brightness, colour distribution, particle density, and spatial position. These features are translated into musical elements, including pitch, volume, rhythm, percussion, and stereo positioning. Built with React, Vite, Tone.js, and the Web Audio API, Sonic Space generates dynamic soundscapes synchronized with corresponding visual data in the browser.

The prototype features three environmental demonstrations: nighttime lights (2012–2023), GEOS atmospheric aerosols, and ISS lightning (2017–2023). It also incorporates captions, legends, data tables, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader-friendly descriptions to support inclusive interaction.

By enabling users to hear environmental patterns and changes rather than relying solely on visual interpretation, Sonic Space creates new opportunities for accessible scientific exploration. It benefits people with visual impairments while offering sighted audiences a multisensory way to understand Earth's changing systems. Ultimately, it makes Earth science more inclusive, engaging, and accessible to diverse audiences.
details:
Sonic Space: Hear the Planet Change

Sonic Space is an interactive, browser-based platform that transforms NASA Earth observation visualizations into immersive, synchronized soundscapes through data-driven sonification. It works by extracting environmental features from NASA visualization frames, including brightness, colour distribution, particle density, and spatial position, and translating them into musical elements such as pitch, volume, rhythm, percussion, and stereo positioning. This enables users to explore environmental phenomena through both sight and sound.

The platform currently demonstrates three Earth science stories: nighttime lights (2012–2023), GEOS atmospheric aerosols, and ISS lightning (2017–2023). Users can explore these visualizations alongside generated audio, supported by captions, audio legends, data tables, and accessibility features.

The project was developed using Python, NumPy, Pillow, and FFmpeg for data processing, and React, Vite, Tone.js, and the Web Audio API for interactive visualization and audio generation.

Its creativity lies in turning scientific data into an expressive auditory experience, bridging Earth science, music, and technology. Rather than presenting environmental information exclusively through charts, maps, and images, Sonic Space makes patterns and changes audible. This is particularly valuable for blind and low-vision individuals, while also offering sighted audiences a new multisensory approach to scientific discovery.

During development, the team considered scientific relevance, meaningful data-to-sound mapping, audio-visual synchronization, usability, browser compatibility, and accessibility. The intended impact is to democratize access to Earth science, encourage inclusive scientific exploration, and strengthen public awareness of environmental changes through an engaging experience that allows people not only to see the planet change, but also to hear it.
